{
  "description": "Traccar is a Java-based open-source GPS tracking platform backend. It ingests telemetry from 200+ device protocols, stores position history in SQL databases, and exposes a REST API for management. While it includes geofencing logic and alarms, it does not contain a map rendering engine or route computation algorithms; those are handled by the separate Traccar Web App frontend.",
  "version": "unknown",
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "name": "Map Layer Management",
      "capability_id": "CAP.MAP.LAYERS",
      "coverage": "none",
      "evidence_status": "inferred",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "evidence_refs": [
        "README.md@e2e2836a"
      ],
      "notes": "Traccar backend does not render maps or manage map layers (tiles, styles). This functionality resides in the separate Traccar Web App repository. The backend serves data *for* the map but does not implement layer management itself."
    },
    {
      "name": "Geofencing",
      "capability_id": "CAP.TRACK.GEOFENCE",
      "coverage": "partial",
      "evidence_status": "declared",
      "confidence": 0.8,
      "evidence_refs": [
        "README.md@e2e2836a"
      ],
      "notes": "README explicitly lists 'Geofencing functionality' and 'Alarms'. Code for geofence logic exists in the full repo but was not in the sampled excerpts. It likely supports polygon/circle definitions and triggers alarms on entry/exit."
    },
    {
      "name": "Route Computation",
      "capability_id": "CAP.ROUTE.COMPUTE",
      "coverage": "none",
      "evidence_status": "unknown",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "evidence_refs": [],
      "notes": "No evidence of route planning, pathfinding, or navigation algorithms in the backend code or README. Traccar tracks existing routes but does not compute new ones."
    },
    {
      "name": "Position History & Playback",
      "capability_id": "CAP.TRACK.HISTORY",
      "coverage": "full",
      "evidence_status": "declared",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "evidence_refs": [
        "README.md@e2e2836a"
      ],
      "notes": "Core feature of the platform. Stores position data in SQL and provides REST API access for retrieval/playback via the web app."
    },
    {
      "name": "Stale Position Handling",
      "capability_id": "CAP.TRACK.POSITION.STALE",
      "coverage": "partial",
      "evidence_status": "inferred",
      "confidence": 0.7,
      "evidence_refs": [
        "README.md@e2e2836a"
      ],
      "notes": "Implied by 'Real-time GPS tracking' and alarm systems. Typically handled via configuration of position validity intervals or device status updates, but specific stale logic is not visible in the sampled protocol decoders."
    }
  ],

    {
      "name": "REST API",

    },
    {
      "name": "Device Protocol Ingestion",
      "protocol": "TCP/UDP (Binary/Text)",
      "direction": "in",
      "schema_ref": "",
      "evidence_status": "verified"
    }
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "Java 21",
    "Jetty 12.1.14",
    "Jersey 4.0.3",
    "Netty 4.2.19",
    "SQL Database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.)"
  ],
  "runtime": [
    "Java 21"
  ],
  "deployment_constraints": [
    "Requires a relational database (MySQL/PostgreSQL/etc.)",
    "Runs as a Java application (JAR)",
    "Docker image available"
  ],
  "maturity": "stable",
  "adaptation_hours_estimate": 40,
  "adaptation_confidence": "medium",
  "adaptation_assumptions": [
    "Assuming the 'Map Visualization Service' component is intended to be a wrapper or integration layer around Traccar's REST API rather than replacing its core.",
    "Geofencing and History capabilities are accessed via Traccar's existing REST API endpoints."
  ],
  "known_gaps": [
    "No map rendering or tile serving (CAP.MAP.LAYERS)",
    "No route computation/planning algorithms (CAP.ROUTE.COMPUTE)",
    "No native MQTT broker for internal state updates (uses REST/WebSocket for client-facing, TCP/UDP for device-facing)"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "License: Apache 2.0 is permissive but requires attribution.",
    "Maintenance: Traccar backend is mature and stable, but integration with custom map services may require significant frontend work in the separate web app repo."
  ],
  "evidence": [
